items.title: Removing or adding one refusal arrow switches refusal
items.line: One arrow, usually found by averaging harmful minus harmless prompts, turns refusal off when removed and on when added, in many chat models.
items.status: 27 papers, 27 with a measured intervention, 4 with held-out accuracy, 5 against

numbers.label: family papers with a measured intervention (rubric C yes)

quote.text: For harmful instructions, the framework allows the LLM to bypass the refusal for 99% of the proposals

items.technical: A refusal direction, most often a difference of means between harmful and harmless prompt activations at a middle layer and a post-instruction token, removes refusal when ablated and induces it when added across Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral and Phi chat models and in vision-language and masked diffusion models. The limits are stated by the papers themselves. Ablating one direction is not enough in Qwen3 models of 8B parameters and more, whatever the extraction method (P3407). It leaves refusal of requests that are not about harm in place (P2800). Restoring it re-engages refusal only partly under prefill attacks (P1799), and it fails against some wrapped jailbreaks (P2376, P3218).
items.why: Solid within stated limits. 27 family papers report it, all with a measured intervention (rubric C yes), over at least six model families. Every failure found (P3407 for larger Qwen3 models, P2800 for refusals not about harm, P1799 prefill, P2376 and P3218 specific jailbreaks, P1805 answer release, P3514 compliant persona) is a setting the paper itself names, so the claim holds only as qualified here.
items.note: The founding single-direction paper, Arditi et al. (P1475), is outside this reading because its taxonomy use includes attack, and most support papers reproduce its recipe. P3218 is in both lists, since its dominant direction cuts Llama AutoDAN ASR from 0.94 to 0.5 but leaves Qwen at 1.0 (g_coding.json). P3218 steers along a probe SVD direction, not a difference of means. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P2800, P3218).

items.title: Whether a plain statement is true can be read
items.line: A simple reader on the hidden state tells true statements from false ones on held-out items, across many models and topics.
items.status: 20 papers, 9 with a measured intervention, 18 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: General truth direction on mixed affirmative and negated statements, AUROC
Our reading of the truth-plane data, worst held-out topic, affirmative and negated sets
numbers.where: sets 'Truth plane, affirmative topics' and 'Truth plane, negated topics' loso_min

quote.text: we present evidence that at sufficient scale, LLMs linearly represent the truth or falsehood of factual statements.

items.technical: Linear probes and difference-of-means directions fitted on residual-stream activations at the last token of short factual statements separate true from false held-out statements, for example a general truth direction at AUROC 0.98 on a balanced mix of affirmative and negated statements in P1482.
items.why: Solid because 20 papers report it, 18 with held-out accuracy (B yes) and 9 with a measured intervention (C yes), across 10 coded model families (DeepSeek, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, Phi, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen, T5). P0673 and P3306 limit how general the direction is (not all models, not reliably transferable), not whether it reads held-out items of the fitting data, so the claim stands for in-distribution reading.
items.note: The claim is about held-out items from the same kind of statement. How far the direction carries to other statement forms and datasets is contested (see the negation and transfer findings). P3133 itself says "at sufficient scale". P0896 is the unsupervised CCS case and reads weaker than supervised probes. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0673, P3306).

items.title: Models often know more than they say
items.line: Hidden states often hold the right answer, the doubt or the image content that the model output fails to show.
items.status: 41 papers, 27 with a measured intervention, 30 with held-out accuracy, 3 against

quote.text: Yet surprisingly, when explicitly asked to rank the same pairs of numerals, these LLMs achieve only 50–70% accuracy, with worse performance for models whose probes are less effective.

items.technical: Linear probes decode numeral order, narrative incoherence, communicative intent, partner beliefs, privacy norms, hidden source commitment and reward-hacking intent above the model’s own verbal or behavioural performance, so many failures sit in the readout rather than in the representation.
items.why: Solid. At least 3 papers with B yes, many families, and no paper shows the represented information to be absent when behaviour fails, only one counter-case where it is not integrated. Counts. 11 supporting papers, 9 with rubric B yes, 6 with rubric C yes, 8 open model families (API-only families not counted), 10 from 2026, 1 against or limiting.
items.note: P1746 is a counter-case where the information itself fails to reach the answer-relevant directions (numeric sensor data), so the gap is not always in the readout. P0478 adds that the incoherence signal fades by the end of the narrative. Merged from 5 verified findings across other, truth-honesty, uncertainty-hallucination, multimodal-agentic, emotion-bias (othe03, trut05, unce05, mult01, emot22). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0512, P1633, P3560).

items.title: Pushing along an emotion arrow changes emotional output
items.line: Adding an emotion direction to the model while it writes makes the text sound more like that emotion, in many models and even speech systems.
items.status: 48 papers, 48 with a measured intervention, 10 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: emotion-sentiment papers with a measured intervention (rubric C yes)
numbers.where: codes.C.mark over the 63 family ids with emotion-sentiment in taxonomy.json concept, counted by script

numbers.label: held-out emotion steering success

quote.text: On the held-out test set, steering achieves a 91.22% success rate, confirming that the extracted emotion vectors capture contextagnostic representations of emotional expression

items.technical: Adding a mean-difference, probe, PCA, SAE or optimised emotion or sentiment vector to residual activations shifts the judged emotion or sentiment of generations in the intended direction, measured against no-steering baselines.
items.why: Solid by the literature rule. 48 papers report it, 48 with a measured intervention (rubric C yes), over 13 open model families (BERT-family, CLIP/ViT, DeepSeek, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, Phi, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen, T5, Vision-language); the papers that limit it report the limits themselves.
items.note: The effect holds on average. P2440 finds it unstable across games and models, and P2862 finds the steering result reverses on a 0.8B model (see the findings below). Several papers here judge the emotion of the output with another model rather than with people, and P3548 shows such judges can disagree with people about emotional quality. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P2440, P2862).

quote.text: The resulting anchor achieves a held-out test AUROC of 0.996 on harmful versus harmless discrimination

items.technical: Linear probes and difference-of-means directions on residual activations reach high held-out accuracy or AUROC for harmful against harmless text inputs drawn from the fitting distribution, across several open model families. Scores vary with the kind of harm, and a high score does not by itself show that the reader tracks harm rather than wording.
items.why: Twenty papers report it, 19 of them coded B yes in papers.json, over open families including Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, DeepSeek, Falcon and OLMo. The weaker in-distribution results are each qualified by their own authors (P0271 near 79 percent F1, P0483 on toxicity, P1231 in early layers, P1806's own linear baseline).
items.note: Solid only as a measurement on text inputs from the training distribution. P3563 argues near-perfect scores can come from wording differences between the harmful and harmless datasets, so the measurement alone does not show what the reader tracks. Image inputs are the exception, see the image finding. P0395 is outside the 149-paper selection. P1198 and P1059 fit several facets or neuron sets rather than one direction. Merged from 2 verified findings across refusal-safety (rmon00, rste02). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P1799, P3407).

items.title: Toxicity arrows cut toxic output and carry to new prompts
items.line: Pushing against an arrow for toxic text while the model writes lowers toxicity, and it still works on prompt sets it was never fitted on.
items.status: 34 papers, 34 with a measured intervention, 7 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

numbers.label: P1283 Jigsaw toxicity, RTP-fitted vector, Llama-3-8B
P0981 AttaQ average max toxicity, Jigsaw-fitted direction, Llama-2
toxicity papers reading one direction on a held-out prompt source (G1 and G2 yes)
numbers.where: G1, G2 over the support ids

quote.text: using RealToxicityPrompts contrastive vectors to mitigate toxicity on the Jigsaw Toxic Comment dataset

items.technical: Toxicity directions fitted by difference of means, linear probes, class-conditional Gaussians or SAE features, added or projected out during decoding, lower measured toxicity on RealToxicityPrompts and related sets, and a direction fitted on one source (Jigsaw, ToxiGen, APPDIA, self-generated pairs, GPT-written stimuli) transfers to prompt sources it never saw, at some cost in fluency or utility.
items.why: Solid. 34 family papers report toxicity reduction with a measured intervention, 9 of them on a prompt source the direction never saw, over GPT-2, Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral, OPT and others. The utility cost P1550 and the fluency cost P0558 report are qualifications, not failures of the reduction.
items.note: Toxicity is most often one of several concepts in these papers, and nearly all gains are measured against baselines the authors ran themselves. P1864 uses the same kind of vector the other way, to make synthetic abusive dialogue more toxic. P0614 is coded G1 and G2 yes for truthfulness transfer, not toxicity, so it is left out of the transfer count. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0558).

items.title: Truthfulness steering raises TruthfulQA scores
items.line: Nudging activations toward a learned truthful arrow raises TruthfulQA scores, most reliably on multiple choice, often by large margins.
items.status: 29 papers, 29 with a measured intervention, 11 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

numbers.label: ITI on Alpaca, TruthfulQA truthfulness
TruthX average gain over 13 LLMs on TruthfulQA
ITI on LLaMA, TruthfulQA True*Info, baseline against ITI, as P1314 reports it

quote.text: ITI improves its truthfulness from 32.5% to 65.1%.

items.technical: Inference-time intervention along truthful directions (per-head probe or mass-mean shifts, learned offsets, spectral or transport maps) raises TruthfulQA True*Info or MC accuracy over the unsteered model across Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma and other families, for example Alpaca from 32.5 to 65.1 percent under ITI. Open-ended gains are less reliable, since P1314 finds ITI and CAA raise MC accuracy but lower True*Info (ITI 48.24 to 40.31 on LLaMA) and P1089 reports ITI steering giving unstable generations.
items.why: Solid because 29 papers report it, 11 with held-out accuracy (B yes) and 29 with a measured intervention (C yes), across 11 coded model families (CLIP/ViT, DeepSeek, Falcon, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen, Vision-language). The contrary papers each state their limit (P1436 uneven steerability, P1314 and P1089 additive baselines hurting open-ended answers), so the claim stands once it is narrowed to multiple-choice and averaged gains.
items.note: Nearly all of these gains are on TruthfulQA itself under two-fold cross-validation, so they are in-domain. Whether the same directions help on other datasets is the separate, problematic transfer finding. P1436 includes TruthfulQA among its behaviours. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P1089, P1314).

items.title: Pushing harder buys control but costs fluency
items.line: Stronger steering moves the target behaviour further, but past some strength the text gets worse and other skills drop.
items.status: 32 papers, 32 with a measured intervention, 7 with held-out accuracy, 4 against

numbers.label: [persona-sycophancy] MMLU accuracy with and without SAE feature steering, Llama-8B and Llama-70B

quote.text: we observe a consistent trade-off between preference and utility: stronger control increases preference while predictably reducing utility.

items.technical: Across methods, raising steering strength increases the target behaviour while lowering utility, with measured drops in coherence, MMLU accuracy (66 to 46 percent for SAE feature steering on Llama-8B) and unrelated-task accuracy, and raw success rates overstate usable control.
items.why: Solid. 9 papers show it with measured interventions (rubric C yes) on Llama, Qwen, Gemma and Mistral, and the papers reporting little cost (P0153, P0465) test moderate strengths.
items.note: P1336 finds the effect of strength can be non-monotonic. Localised steering (next finding) is the main remedy proposed. Merged from 5 verified findings across persona-sycophancy, other, emotion-bias, refusal-safety, style-language (pers30, othe12, emot04, rste13, styl15).

items.title: Hidden states foretell the answer before any text
items.line: Probes read whether a question is answerable, whether the model will succeed and what it will say before it writes.
items.status: 27 papers, 16 with a measured intervention, 23 with held-out accuracy, 2 against

numbers.label: [other] Jailbreak reduction from the probe early-warning system (P1545)
[task-reasoning] in-distribution AUC of a GSM8K correctness predictor
[task-reasoning] accuracy of arithmetic error detectors
[task-reasoning] share of steps where latent answer commitment and the written answer align
[uncertainty-hallucination] Held-out F1 of the unanswerability direction

quote.text: We provide evidence that there are times when we can predict how an LM will behave early in computation, before even a single token is generated.

items.technical: Linear probes on the final input token or on intermediate reasoning steps forecast prompt leakage, instruction-following failure, jailbreak compliance, answer changes under follow-up, total response length and future behaviours on held-out items, with conformal calibration giving an early-warning system.
items.why: Solid. At least 3 papers with B yes over many families, and the one transfer limit is qualified by its authors. Counts. 6 supporting papers, 6 with rubric B yes, 2 with rubric C yes, 8 open model families (API-only families not counted), 2 from 2026, 1 against or limiting.
items.note: P0958 limits the claim, since its probe does not transfer to held-out instruction types (AUROC 0.50 to 0.55), which its authors state. P0627 picked its best configuration on the held-out strict test set (lt_coding swept-test). Merged from 3 verified findings across other, task-reasoning, uncertainty-hallucination (othe04, task13, unce01). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0958).

items.title: Pushing one concept moves other behaviours too
items.line: Steering along one concept direction often shifts related traits, values or skills, because the directions overlap.
items.status: 28 papers, 28 with a measured intervention, 10 with held-out accuracy, 2 against

numbers.label: [persona-sycophancy] our map, Big-5 openness against extraversion, plain and whitened pooled cosine
numbers.where: pooled.cos and pooled.cos_white at order entries Big-5 Chat, openness and Big-5 Chat, extraversion

[persona-sycophancy] target to cross-trait effect ratio
[emotion-bias] refusal on OKTest when arousal is pushed down
[truth-honesty] MMLU on LLaMA under ITI, as P2243 reports it

quote.text: steering one trait consistently induces changes in others, even when linear overlap is explicitly removed.

items.technical: Big Five, value, empathy-mechanism and behaviour directions are geometrically coupled, and steering one produces measurable off-target shifts in others, even after linear overlap is removed, with the size of the spillover disputed.
items.why: Solid that spillover exists. 10 papers show off-target effects with measured interventions (rubric C yes) on Llama, Qwen, Mistral, Gemma and OLMo, and our exploratory map shows the Big-5 directions far more aligned than unrelated datasets. Only the size is contested.
items.note: P0711 finds the largest off-target effect often comparable to the target effect, while P1083 finds cross-effects about one ninth of target effects and calls the traits approximately orthogonal, though it also reports non-orthogonal correlations. Our map figures are exploratory, at one reading (Llama-3-8B-Instruct, layer 16, last token), with no registered prediction. Merged from 4 verified findings across persona-sycophancy, other, emotion-bias, truth-honesty (pers09, othe16, emot05, trut04). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P1314).

items.title: Directions often carry over between related models
items.line: A direction found in a base model often still works in its chat-tuned version or a close relative.
items.status: 27 papers, 26 with a measured intervention, 12 with held-out accuracy, 5 against

numbers.label: [truth-honesty] Reasoning against recall direction before and after GRPO, mean-direction cosine (Qwen3-0.6B)
[truth-honesty] MMLU linear probe on teacher against ternary model

quote.text: In other words, fine-tuning recombines existing concepts rather than learning new ones.

items.technical: Base-model SAE features and axes explain chat-tuned and RL-tuned behaviour (feature drift, a pre-existing welfare axis, crosscoder latents present in both), a steering vector built on the base model works on the tuned model, subliminal fine-tuning recovers the teacher vector, and affine or autoencoder maps transfer steering vectors, probes and SAEs across sizes and families.
items.why: Solid. At least 3 papers with C yes over many families, and the two limits are qualified by their authors. Counts. 11 supporting papers, 4 with rubric B yes, 11 with rubric C yes, 12 open model families (API-only families not counted), 7 from 2026, 2 against or limiting.
items.note: P0336 limits the reuse claim to RL, finding that SFT rapidly introduces many specialised features. P1602 finds a transferred language-steering vector works for some languages but not others, and says so. Merged from 3 verified findings across other, uncertainty-hallucination, truth-honesty (othe10, unce11, trut07). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0336, P1602).

items.title: A few heads, neurons or features can carry the steering
items.line: Steering only a handful of attention heads, neurons or dictionary features often matches pushing the whole hidden state.
items.status: 30 papers, 30 with a measured intervention, 6 with held-out accuracy, 4 against

numbers.label: [persona-sycophancy] share of dense effectiveness with a sparse mask, and dimensions used
[refusal-safety] P3135 share of DPO toxicity reduction from dampened toxic neurons

quote.text: intervention targeting only these specific heads achieves robust behavioral control while significantly mitigating the coherency degradation observed in residual stream steering.

items.technical: Sparse or localised interventions (three style-modulation heads, about 0.5 percent of MLP neurons, 10 to 30 percent of dimensions via learned masks, sparse SAE steering, a sparse set of middle-layer heads for sycophancy) reach 97 to 100 percent of dense effectiveness or better, often with less loss of coherence or capability.
items.why: Solid. 10 papers show it with measured interventions (rubric C yes) on Gemma, Llama, Qwen and Mistral, while P2373 finds an automated commercial SAE feature steerer costs much accuracy, which limits the claim for that kind of feature selection.
items.note: Most comparisons are against residual-stream CAA on the same concept and model, and few report held-out accuracy. P0650 finds SAE value steering changes fewer unintended values than role prompts. Merged from 3 verified findings across persona-sycophancy, refusal-safety, other (pers31, rste07, othe08). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0557).

items.title: Whether the model's own answer is right can be read
items.line: A simple reader on the model's hidden state tells right answers from wrong ones on new questions from the same dataset, usually well above chance.
items.status: 28 papers, 9 with a measured intervention, 25 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: [uncertainty-hallucination] Correctness probe AUC across 11 models
[uncertainty-hallucination] Hallucination detection AUROC of the truthfulness separator vector on TruthfulQA, Llama-3.1-8b, 32 labelled examples

quote.text: A correctness probe reaches 0.80–0.97 AUC across the 11 models

items.technical: Linear probes or class-mean directions fit on hidden states classify the correctness of the model's own answer on held-out items of the fitting dataset, with AUROC of 0.80 to 0.97 across 11 models in P3560 and 84.2 percent on TruthfulQA for P1211's separator vector.
items.why: Solid because 27 papers report it, 24 with held-out accuracy (B yes) and 9 with a measured intervention (C yes), the coded model families of these papers span 9 families (CLIP/ViT, DeepSeek, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, Phi, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen), and the 2 papers that limit it (P0277, P2563) bound the size of the effect and say so rather than showing it fail unqualified.
items.note: The claim is in-domain only (fit and test on one dataset). P2563 finds a modest correctness probe, about 0.66 (runs/soundness/survey_search/fulltext/txt/P2563.txt lines 616-617), no better than behavioural confidence, and P0277 finds AUC near chance on the subset where two models disagree, so both limit the size of the effect rather than overturn it. P1575 reports only the unsupervised CCS baseline, which reads weaker. P0433, P0772 and P1726 give B partial only. P3205 and P3359 are two versions of one paper, so the 27 supporting records are 26 distinct works. Merged from 2 verified findings across uncertainty-hallucination, truth-honesty (unce00, trut01). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0277, P1575, P2563).

items.title: Which token you read changes what you find
items.line: The same probe can look strong or weak depending on which word of the question or answer it reads.
items.status: 20 papers, 10 with a measured intervention, 20 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: Family papers that compare read positions (T2 yes)
numbers.where: rows[id].T2 over the 101 family ids selected from SURVEY/data/taxonomy.json

quote.text: truthfulness information is concentrated in the exact answer tokens

items.technical: Correctness and uncertainty information concentrates at specific positions (exact answer tokens, the first decoded token, the post-answer newline, the last token of a claim), and papers comparing positions find large differences in detection.
items.why: Solid because 20 papers report it, 20 with held-out accuracy (B yes) and 10 with a measured intervention (C yes), the coded model families of these papers span 11 families (CLIP/ViT, DeepSeek, Falcon, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OPT, Phi, Qwen, T5, Vision-language), and no paper in the family shows it failing.
items.note: The best position differs between papers, so the robust claim is that position matters, not which position wins. P3205 and P3359 are two versions of one paper, so the 20 supporting records are 19 distinct works.

items.title: A truthful minus hallucinated direction cuts text hallucination
items.line: In text models, nudging activations toward the truthful side lowers hallucination on the kind of benchmark the direction was built from.
items.status: 23 papers, 23 with a measured intervention, 7 with held-out accuracy, 3 against

numbers.label: TruthfulQA MC1 change when editing along plus and minus the truthful direction
Hallucination reduction on short-form QA

quote.text: editing with δ brings 20% MC1 improvements and editing with −δ results in a 19% MC1 drop

items.technical: Adding a truthful-minus-hallucinated direction (mean difference, spectral edit, optimised BiPO vector, rotation or amortised into weights) raises TruthfulQA scores or lowers short-form QA hallucination rates in-distribution, and subtracting it raises hallucination.
items.why: Solid because 23 papers report it, 7 with held-out accuracy (B yes) and 23 with a measured intervention (C yes), the coded model families of these papers span 9 families (Falcon, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, OPT, Phi, Qwen, Vision-language), and the 4 papers that limit it qualify their claims or bound the size of the effect rather than showing it fail unqualified.
items.note: P3295 and P1320 find extrinsic hallucination largely unsteerable in Gemma-2-2B and Qwen and say so, P2702 reports static vectors backfiring out of distribution and says so, and P0486 finds robustness under shift fails, so the failures come with qualified claims. P2702 appears on both sides because its SVF succeeds where its CAA and BiPO baselines fail. Our own registered test found the CAA hallucination arrow inert at layer 16 of Llama-3-8B-Instruct (see the shaky finding on our steering test). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P2702).

items.title: Task vectors can stand in for in-context examples
items.line: A vector read from worked examples can replace the examples in the prompt, in text models and in vision-language models.
items.status: 25 papers, 25 with a measured intervention, 2 with held-out accuracy, 2 against

numbers.label: [task-reasoning] zero-shot task accuracy with an instruction function vector added, best models
[multimodal-agentic] P1224 gain of text-example task-vector patching over text-example prompting on image queries

quote.text: Thus, ICL can be seen as compressing S into a single task vector θ(S) and then using this task vector to modulate the transformer to produce the output.

items.technical: Hidden states or summed attention-head outputs taken from few-shot prompts (task vectors and function vectors), when patched or added into a zero-shot forward pass, raise accuracy on the demonstrated task well above zero-shot and often close to few-shot, shown by measured interventions on simple word tasks in some GPT-J, Pythia, Llama, Gemma, Mistral, OLMo and Qwen models.
items.why: Reported by 20 family papers with measured interventions (rubric C yes) across at least seven model families. P0204, the main sceptic, reproduces the effect on GPT-J where it was first shown. The failures other papers report are stated as limits of task type or model, and the next two findings cover them.
items.note: Solid as a claim that such vectors exist and work on the models and simple word tasks where they were shown. It does not extend to most other models (P0204) or to rule-inference tasks (P0734, P1113). Several papers here use head sums or raw hidden states rather than a fitted contrast. Merged from 2 verified findings across task-reasoning, multimodal-agentic (task00, mult10). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0734, P0769, P1113, P1460).

items.title: Bias steering lowers benchmark bias on average
items.line: Adding or editing along a bias direction makes models score less biased on standard bias tests, at least on average.
items.status: 19 papers, 19 with a measured intervention, 7 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: average improvement of per-axis steering vectors on BBQ, CLEAR-Bias and StereoSet
bias-demographics papers with a measured intervention (rubric C yes)
numbers.where: codes.C.mark over the 52 family ids with bias-demographics in taxonomy.json concept, counted by script

quote.text: compared to the base model, our method effectively improves accuracy and reduces bias scores in both ambiguous and disambiguated contexts across all tested models, in both zero-shot and few-shot settings

items.technical: Mean-difference, PCA, probe and optimised bias directions applied at inference reduce BBQ, StereoSet, CrowS-Pairs, Winogenerated or occupational bias scores relative to base and prompting baselines across several model families.
items.why: Solid by the literature rule for the average effect. 19 papers report it, 19 with a measured intervention, over 9 open model families (BERT-family, DeepSeek, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, Qwen, Vision-language); the papers that limit it show group-level exceptions, not a failed average.
items.note: The gain shrinks off the fitting benchmark, as P0792 shows (12.8% on BBQ against 1% on StereoSet). The group-level failures are the next finding. P0647 finds steering for truthfulness costs fairness, so the direction steered matters. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0108, P0792, P1478).

items.title: Style, register and figurative arrows steer how text reads
items.line: Adding a style arrow makes replies more Shakespearean, formal, analogical, metaphorical or personal, and in one control a random arrow does nothing.
items.status: 19 papers, 19 with a measured intervention, 5 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

quote.text: On Shakespeare-style benchmark, DRESS exhibits 7.84% improvements on overall assessment and 1.37% on GPT-4 rating compared to the best-performing baseline.

items.technical: Mean-difference, probe, SVD-subspace or SAE style directions added during generation raise style scores for Shakespeare, formality, conceptual complexity, analogy, verse, personal and translator style, metaphor and literalness, and code-library choice.
items.why: Solid by the literature rule. 19 family ids report it (18 separate works, P3186 is likely an earlier version of P0389), 5 with held-out accuracy (rubric B yes) and 19 with a measured intervention (rubric C yes), over 10 open model families (BERT-family, DeepSeek, Falcon, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, Qwen, Vision-language). P1141 finds humor and appropriateness hard to elicit but qualifies this as concept-specific, so no unqualified failure is on record.
items.note: P0778 notes that factual prompts barely move under style vectors, and P2697 that rare code libraries are harder to induce than common ones. The cost of strong steering is a separate finding.

items.title: Sparse autoencoder features can flag and steer concepts
items.line: Single features from sparse dictionaries can detect and steer refusal, toxicity, hallucination and visual concepts.
items.status: 20 papers, 19 with a measured intervention, 4 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

numbers.label: [multimodal-agentic] P1192 seed stability of SAE directions on the Paulo and Belrose metric, decoder/encoder, Matryoshka (RW) and best listed row
numbers.where: Table 18 lines 5734-5825, Matryoshka (RW) at line 5786 and TopK (k = 64) at line 5771 (column order Sparsity, Reconstruction, Stability per the header at lines 5734-5738)

quote.text: Causal interventions using these features confirm that they mediate refusal

items.technical: Refusal and toxicity can be steered through SAE decoder features. A direction rebuilt from 64 SAE features picked on the chat model's activations matches the true refusal direction under ablation, while features picked on the base model fail (P0787). Toxicity is cut by up to 20 percent (P0558), sparse SAS vectors steer refusal on Gemma 2 (P0382) and safety-relevant features move Claude 3 Sonnet outputs (P2646), while feature splitting in wider SAEs weakens detoxification (P0558) and spreads useful features across neighbours (P2030).
items.why: Solid. Seven family papers with measured interventions over Gemma, GPT-2, Llama and Claude. Feature splitting is a limit the papers themselves report, and P0202's token-tracking latents are a caution on how features are selected.
items.note: P2376 finds prior global feature explanations fail to restore refusal on specific jailbreaks even after 20 changes, while its local selection needs about six. Merged from 3 verified findings across refusal-safety, uncertainty-hallucination, multimodal-agentic (rste23, unce08, mult14). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P1071, P3215).

items.title: A direction controls how long models think
items.line: Reflection, length or confidence directions make reasoning models think longer or shorter when pushed.
items.status: 18 papers, 18 with a measured intervention, 5 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: [task-reasoning] reasoning tokens cut by SEAL
[task-reasoning] reasoning tokens saved by ReflCtrl on MMLU subsets
[task-reasoning] average generated tokens cut by ReBalance
[uncertainty-hallucination] Reasoning tokens saved on MMLU subsets

quote.text: Our analysis reveals that reasoning length is governed by a linear direction in the representation space

items.technical: Difference-of-means or PCA directions separating reflection or transition steps from execution steps, long from short chains, or slow from fast thinking, added or subtracted at step boundaries, cut reasoning tokens by roughly 10 to 50 percent at similar accuracy, or lengthen reasoning, in DeepSeek-R1 distilled Qwen and Llama models, QwQ and Qwen3.
items.why: Reported by 17 family papers, several with held-out accuracy of the direction (P0418, P1504, P1634 B yes) and all with measured interventions, across DeepSeek, Qwen and Llama families. The limits other papers find are stated as limits.
items.note: P1639 finds the SEAL vector does not shorten AIME24 traces for two models, P3529 finds code barely responds, and P2559 finds most keyword-labelled boundaries unstable, which dilutes these vectors. Most of these models are DeepSeek-R1 distillations of Qwen or Llama. Merged from 2 verified findings across task-reasoning, uncertainty-hallucination (task08, unce10). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P1639, P1691, P2559, P3529).

items.title: Emotion and sentiment can be read off hidden states
items.line: A simple straight-line reader on the model's hidden states tells emotions and positive from negative apart on held-out text, often almost perfectly.
items.status: 16 papers, 12 with a measured intervention, 11 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

numbers.label: binary affect probe AUROC on keyword-free clinical vignettes, six models
27-class GoEmotions accuracy of zero-shot emotion directions, peak layer

quote.text: Gemma-2-9B exhibited significantly higher activation separability compared to Mistral-7B, with mean test accuracies in the >0.9 range across all layers compared to ∼0.55 to ∼0.89 in Mistral-7B.

items.technical: Linear probes or projections onto emotion and sentiment directions classify held-out items by emotion, affect or polarity at high accuracy across several open model families, with binary affect detection near ceiling and fine-grained categories harder.
items.why: Solid by the literature rule. 16 papers in the family report it, 11 with held-out accuracy (rubric B yes), over 11 open model families (BERT-family, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, Phi, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen, T5, Vision-language), and no paper shows it failing without qualification.
items.note: Strength depends on the model and the task. P0408 finds Mistral-7B at about 0.55 to 0.89 against Gemma above 0.9. P2025 reads 27 fine-grained GoEmotions labels only at 37.2% at best (its random baseline is 8.2% per our coding), which limits the claim for fine categories. P0292, P0778, P1250 and P1237 give separability without a stated held-out split (B partial). P1053 reads emotions on other corpora than it fit on, which is transfer rather than held-out accuracy. Sentiment polarity is read at AUROC 95.7 from Sentence-T5 embeddings (P0638), a sentiment feedback signal at 99.80% or more from SAE features (P1456 per our coding), and sentiment classes from frozen BERT after continual learning (P0895).

items.title: Steering cuts made-up objects in vision-language models
items.line: Directions built for hallucination cut how often vision-language models describe objects that are not in the image.
items.status: 18 papers, 18 with a measured intervention, 5 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

numbers.label: [multimodal-agentic] P1316 CHAIRs on LLaVA-1.5-7B, before and after steering
[multimodal-agentic] Family papers reporting a hallucination direction that reduces hallucination with a measured intervention
numbers.value: 15 papers, all C yes, 5 B yes
numbers.where: codes.C.mark and codes.B.mark for the 15 support ids

numbers.label: [multimodal-agentic] P1548 POPE adversarial accuracy on LLaVA-v1.5, no steering vs a single mean steering vector
numbers.where: lines 783-792 (Table 2, columns No-steering then Prompt, Norm-Rnd, Mean-S)

numbers.label: [multimodal-agentic] P0858 POPE adversarial accuracy/F1 on LLaVA-1.5-7B, zero-shot vs CAA baseline
numbers.where: lines 697-700 (Table 1 row order Zero-shot, ML-ACT, MLLM Steering, CAA)

numbers.label: [uncertainty-hallucination] Hallucination reduction by orthogonalising image features

quote.text: interventions along the identified faithful direction can mitigate hallucinations, while those along the hallucinatory direction can exacerbate them

items.technical: Contrastive directions fitted on faithful versus hallucinated VLM states (difference of means, PCA of paired differences, SAE latents, Wiener-filter eigenmodes, or orthogonal erasure of object features) lower CHAIR and POPE hallucination when added or projected at inference, including when fitted on one image set such as COCO or MIMIC-CXR and applied to another, and linear probes on the same states separate hallucinated from faithful tokens on held-out data. A plain averaged contrast vector does not reliably help, since a mean steering vector does no better than no steering on POPE adversarial in P1548 and a CAA baseline falls well below the unsteered model in P0858, so the result belongs to purpose-built estimators with tuned layers and strengths.
items.why: Solid for the scoped claim. 15 family papers report it, all 15 with a measured intervention (C yes) and 5 with held-out accuracy (P0160, P0601, P0859, P0975, P1316 B yes), over Llama-based LLaVA, Qwen, Gemma and CLIP-based models per papers.json model_families. The limits are either qualified by their authors (P0160, P1048 and P1548 say one fixed or averaged vector is not enough), outside the CHAIR and POPE scope (P0859 on LLaVA-Bench), or a baseline failure that the scoping to purpose-built methods absorbs (P0858).
items.note: P0160, P1048 and P0859 appear in both lists because their own results support the core claim and limit its reach. P1548 and P0858 are vision-language papers coded to hallucination but not to visual-multimodal, so the family selection missed them. P0858 reports CAA only as a baseline and does not qualify anything, so treating it as scoping rather than refuting is a judgment call. Detection accuracy is modest where given, 66.67 to 72.99 percent against about 50 for a random latent in P0859 (SURVEY/data/papers.json, P0859 codes.B.where, read from a figure by our coder), and POPE gains can be small, SHARP moving POPE adversarial accuracy on LLaVA-1.5 from 75.8 to 76.8 (SURVEY/data/g_coding.json, P0601 groups_read). Steering strength trades hallucination against recall (P1232, P1316). No paper here checks that the direction is stable when refitted (A yes in none), and P0601, P1019 and P1048 pick layer, heads or strength on the evaluation benchmark (our layer coding). Merged from 2 verified findings across multimodal-agentic, uncertainty-hallucination (mult00, unce03). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0160, P0859, P1048, P1548).

items.technical: Refits of supervised directions on subsamples, seeds or feature datasets agree closely (about 99% alignment after 50 samples, high cosine across seeds and feature corpora, stable ridge-probe axes, bootstrap LDA stability that predicts steerability), yet only 9 of the 145 papers in this family report such a check.
items.why: Solid for supervised directions within one data set. At least 3 papers with rubric A yes over at least 2 families, and the contrary paper concerns SAE dictionaries, a different estimator. Counts. 6 supporting papers, 3 with rubric B yes, 5 with rubric C yes, 9 open model families (API-only families not counted), 4 from 2026, 1 against or limiting.
items.note: Stability within one data set says nothing about agreement across groups. The survey notes that P1348’s check compares a running vector with the final one, which agree by construction (SURVEY/paper/sections/evidence.tex lines 215 to 217). SAE dictionaries are the exception (P1097, see the problematic finding). Another 38 of the 145 are coded partial on rubric A (SURVEY/data/papers.json codes.A.mark, script count). Merged from 4 verified findings across other, cross-cutting, task-reasoning, style-language (othe17, prac09, task06, styl02).

items.title: Gender lies along a readable line that projection removes
items.line: A model stores gender along a straight line, so a simple reader finds it, it carries across tasks, and projecting it out blinds that reader.
items.status: 16 papers, 14 with a measured intervention, 8 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

numbers.label: in-language gender classifier accuracy, mBERT, English

quote.text: In-language, the accuracy of gender prediction drops to majority after applying INLP, while profession classification is only slightly hurt.

items.technical: Gender is linearly decodable from word, sentence and residual representations at high held-out accuracy, a single gender vector transfers across tasks and languages, and nullspace or projection erasure drops linear gender decodability to chance.
items.why: Solid by the literature rule. 16 papers report linear gender directions, 8 with held-out accuracy and 14 with a measured intervention, over 9 open model families (BERT-family, CLIP/ViT, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen); the limits are stated by the papers that found them.
items.note: Solid for linear decodability and its removal, not for removing bias (next finding). P0811 is listed on both sides because a linear probe falls to 48.7% after erasure while bias indicators barely move. P0171 finds speech translation models built with adapters encode little speaker gender and default to masculine forms. P1020 finds that sparse autoencoders with non-negative codes split the male and female poles into separate features. Many of these papers use BERT-family encoders. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0811).

items.title: Pushing along an unknown direction switches abstention on and off
items.line: Adding an 'I do not know' direction makes the model refuse or abstain, and subtracting it makes the model answer.
items.status: 12 papers, 12 with a measured intervention, 6 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: Abstention when the unanswerability direction is subtracted at alpha minus 2
Abstention of a non-expert role after adding the confidence vector

quote.text: increasing the unknown entity latent induces almost 100% refusal across all entity types in Gemma 2 2B

items.technical: Adding or subtracting a direction for unanswerability, unknown entities, ambiguity, missing visual evidence or low confidence at a middle layer raises or lowers the model's abstention or refusal rate, in both directions of the push.
items.why: Solid because 12 papers report it, 6 with held-out accuracy (B yes) and 12 with a measured intervention (C yes), the coded model families of these papers span 10 families (CLIP/ViT, DeepSeek, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen, Vision-language), and no paper in the family shows it failing.
items.note: The push moves abstention on answerable questions too, so it is not specific to the unknown items. That side effect is the problematic steering finding below. P2690 moves false-premise detection rather than abstention and is a close relative.

items.title: Numeric and relational facts sit on editable lines
items.line: Facts like birth years, map positions and dates lie along straight lines inside the model, and moving along them changes the answer.
items.status: 13 papers, 11 with a measured intervention, 7 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

numbers.label: Birthyear patch, correlation with expressed year, Llama 2 13B

quote.text: LLMs learn linear representations of space and time across multiple scales.

items.technical: Low-dimensional linear directions (ridge or PLS probes, linear relational embeddings) encode entity attributes such as latitude, longitude, dates and birth years, and patching along them changes the expressed value or comparison outcome, for example a birthyear patch that tracks the output at correlation 0.84 on Llama 2 13B.
items.why: Solid because 13 papers report it, 7 with held-out accuracy (B yes) and 11 with a measured intervention (C yes), across 8 coded model families (Falcon, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen). The against papers show where the line is weak (latitude in P1387, arbitrary output codes in P2101, the death state under role-play in P1501) and each says so, so the claim holds with those limits.
items.note: P2101 finds the country-continent content transfers to adjective answers but only 1 of 5, 0 of 4 and 0 of 2 qualified maps to arbitrary codes (line 1495). P1501 finds the dead or alive state read at about 85 percent in role-play against nearly 100 percent without it (lines 642-643). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P1387, P2101).

items.title: Steering cuts sycophancy on the data it was built for
items.line: Pushing the model's state away from a sycophancy direction makes it give in to users less often, on data like its training data.
items.status: 13 papers, 13 with a measured intervention, 5 with held-out accuracy, 2 against

numbers.label: PAS monotonicity and mean shift per direction against baselines
peak mitigation of clinical sycophancy, MedGemma-27B

quote.text: PAS achieves strong monotonicity (Spearman ρ = +0.92) and an average shift of 15.4% per direction, compared with 8.7% for the baselines.

items.technical: Subtracting or rescaling sycophancy directions or PCA subspaces, adding probe-derived head vectors, reweighting heads, or ablating a few heads or neurons reduces measured sycophancy in distribution, with monotone bidirectional control (Spearman 0.92) in one method, on Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral and video-language models.
items.why: Solid in distribution. All 13 support papers report a measured intervention (rubric C yes) over Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral, OLMo and video-language models, and the two limiting papers show side effects rather than a failure to reduce sycophancy.
items.note: Effects range from large (P0411) to modest (P3105 at 21.9 percent). P2477 and P3437 act by silencing neurons or heads rather than adding a vector, and in P3437 silencing the error-signal heads raises sycophancy. Transfer to other datasets is weaker (next finding).

items.title: Pushing along the truth direction flips true and false
items.line: Adding or subtracting the truth arrow inside the model makes it treat false statements as true and the other way round.
items.status: 10 papers, 10 with a measured intervention, 9 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: Mass-mean direction more causal than LR and CCS
Error-rate swing from steering along the correctness direction on Qwen2-7B-Instruct, TruthfulQA
numbers.value: 9.1 percentage points (0.61 at alpha -5, 0.52 at alpha +5, baseline 0.56)

quote.text: intervening in a LLM’s forward pass, causing it to treat false statements as true and vice versa.

items.technical: Adding a scaled difference-of-means or probe truth direction to the residual stream during the forward pass shifts the model's true or false judgement or answer error rate, with mass-mean directions more causal than logistic-regression or CCS directions in 7 of 8 conditions in P3133 and random or orthogonal controls near baseline in P3560.
items.why: Solid because 10 papers report it, 9 with held-out accuracy (B yes) and 10 with a measured intervention (C yes), across 6 coded model families (GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen). P2305 is listed against only because the same kind of steering can have the opposite behavioural effect later in a conversation, which qualifies rather than refutes the causal role.
items.note: Most tests use short true or false statements or multiple-choice answers. P2305 reports that steering on pre-answer representations can yield opposite behavioural changes at different points in a conversation. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P2305).

items.title: Some concepts need more than one direction
items.line: For some tasks and concepts one direction falls short, and several directions or a small subspace work better.
items.status: 13 papers, 12 with a measured intervention, 3 with held-out accuracy

quote.text: We show that contextual privacy in LLMs is not a single direction but a multi-dimensional subspace aligned with Contextual Integrity theory.

items.technical: Contextual privacy splits into three independent CI axes, multinomial and temporal concepts form affine subspaces, circles and lines, list indexing uses a 3D channel, genealogy a cone subspace and relation types a polar code, and steering along a fitted manifold gives more natural outputs than a straight line.
items.why: Solid. At least 3 papers with C yes over many families, and no paper in this family shows these concepts to be captured fully by one direction. Counts. 8 supporting papers, 3 with rubric B yes, 7 with rubric C yes, 9 open model families (API-only families not counted), 5 from 2026, 0 against or limiting.
items.note: P3453 has no full-text file in the fulltext folder, so it is listed from its coded record only and not quoted. P0409 is secondary for directions, since its own method is nonlinear. Merged from 2 verified findings across other, task-reasoning (othe11, task02). The family readers placed these under problematic, solid; the editor placed the merged item under solid.

items.technical: Papers locate truth, knowledge-boundary and conflict signals in middle layers, and our registered depth sweep finds the shared truth direction (positive cosine between the larger-than and smaller-than directions, transfer near 1.0) forms between 0.31 and 0.375 of depth in Llama-3-8B, between 0.4 and 0.5 in Qwen2.5-14B and between 0.6 and 0.7 in Qwen2.5-72B.
items.why: Solid because 11 papers report it, 9 with held-out accuracy (B yes) and 8 with a measured intervention (C yes), across 7 coded model families (Falcon, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen). Our part is solid under the rule for our own results, since the depth sweep was registered before capture (RUNLOG entry 2026-09-24 0955) and all five predictions held with the falsifier not fired (scored in the 1030 entry).
items.note: The sweep covers truth items only (the 8 statement types of P3133 and the affirmative and negated relation templates of P1482) and locates the flip only between sampled layers. The corpus reads Qwen at about 0.4 of depth, before the shared arrow forms, so our Llama-against-Qwen differences on truth data are partly a layer effect. Qwen2.5-72B was read in 4-bit.

items.title: Targeted steering cuts over-refusal and keeps real refusals
items.line: Steering applied only when needed, or per category, makes models refuse fewer harmless requests while still refusing harmful ones.
items.status: 13 papers, 13 with a measured intervention, 2 with held-out accuracy, 2 against

numbers.label: SCANS cut in false refusal, XSTest and OKTest
supporting papers coded C yes

quote.text: conditioning a behavior vector vrefusal on condition vector charmful selectively increases refusal rates for harmful content while leaving harmless prompt refusal rates largely unchanged

items.technical: Conditioning refusal steering on a harmfulness detector, an input-dependent coefficient or a benign null space lowers false refusal on benign-looking prompts while keeping refusal on standard harmful benchmarks, across several model families.
items.why: Ten papers report it with measured interventions (all ten C yes) over Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, Phi and DeepSeek. P0486 confirms that refusal on standard harmful queries is kept, so no paper shows the narrow claim failing.
items.note: P0486 shows that steering to cut over-refusal can lower robustness to jailbreak-wrapped harmful queries, which most gated papers test only as attack defence rates. P1219 tests refusal under an adversarial suffix rather than over-refusal, and P1309 corrects over-refusal by projection rather than a detector, so both are weaker support. P0306 is outside the 149-paper selection. Merged from 2 verified findings across refusal-safety (rmon07, rste22). The family readers placed these under shaky, solid; the editor placed the merged item under solid. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P2104).

quote.text: for each model, we find a single direction such that erasing this direction from the model’s residual stream activations prevents it from refusing harmful instructions

items.technical: Group directions of five harmful-request datasets (Arditi training sources and harm categories, PolyRefuse languages, P0334 categories, P0819 languages) have a cross-dataset median cosine of 0.814 over 824 group pairs at Llama-3-8B-Instruct layer 16, last token, and in a registered construction XSTest and OR-Bench benign look-alikes are ranked below their harmful counterparts as whole sets at 0.987 to 0.995 and 0.918 to 0.924 under three refusal and harmfulness directions, so the registered flip predictions PB1 to PB3 all failed and the falsifier fired, the outcome stated in advance as expected.
items.why: Solid under our rule, the median is a direct count that the checkers found survives length and ending matching, near duplicates and removing shared components, and the flip test was registered (RUNLOG 2026-09-22 12.08) with nothing-to-flip as the stated expectation, which held on three directions (scored 12.12).
items.note: One model family (Llama-3 and Llama-3.1). The shared Alpaca harmless pool inflates agreement modestly (arditi_cat with arditi_src 0.958 to 0.874 with matched benign rewrites, striking_links.json surviving entry 3). Where the arrow fades it is in languages the model barely reads, Yoruba at 0.196 and Chichewa at 0.224 against the pooled arditi_src direction, which P1571 and P0819 also report. P2800, P1215 and P1542 argue refusal is carried by several directions, or that harmfulness and refusal differ; they test mediation or other token positions, which our read-out count at the last token does not test, so they limit a one-mechanism reading rather than contradict the count. PB5 also failed for the whole OR-Bench group (0.938 to 0.966). P2800's rebuilt dataset is one of the four dropped. Merged from 2 verified findings across cross-cutting, refusal-safety (ours03, rste16). The family readers placed these under new, solid; the editor placed the merged item under solid. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P2800).

items.title: Sycophancy can be read off activations on new items
items.line: A simple linear reader on the model's internal state tells sycophantic from honest answers well on new examples like its training ones.
items.status: 9 papers, 5 with a measured intervention, 9 with held-out accuracy, 2 against

numbers.label: residual-stream probe accuracy, Gemma-3 layer 15
sycophancy probe five-fold CV AUROC

quote.text: For Gemma-3, the residual stream reaches 99.6% accuracy at layer 15, while MLP probes peak at 97.3% around layer 10.

items.technical: Linear probes and difference-of-means directions separate sycophantic from non-sycophantic responses at high held-out accuracy or AUROC within the fitting distribution (99.6 percent at Gemma-3 layer 15, AUROC 0.949 under five-fold cross-validation, 90.3 percent for one mean-difference direction), on Llama, Gemma, Qwen and GPT-2.
items.why: Solid in distribution. All 9 support papers report held-out accuracy (rubric B yes) over Llama, Gemma, Qwen and GPT-2 among others, and the papers that show the reader failing do so under a changed setting and say so.
items.note: Holds only in distribution. P0322 uses 30 matched pairs per model. P2001 reports a more modest AUC of 0.81 on held-out topics. P0403 reads a related belief-flip state. P3451 appears in both lists, since it reports a strong baseline and then shows it collapses once revealing text is removed (see the finding on textual evidence). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P3451).

items.title: Steering for other goals can change safety
items.line: Pushing a persona, a mood or another goal can weaken or switch the model refusals as a side effect.
items.status: 11 papers, 10 with a measured intervention, 1 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: [persona-sycophancy] change in attack success rate from CAA behaviour steering
[persona-sycophancy] worst-case attack success increase from steering
[persona-sycophancy] Llama refusal rate under compliant-persona steering

quote.text: We demonstrate that steering, even with random vectors, reliably breaks alignment safeguards across multiple model families, inducing harmful compliance rates of 1–13%.

items.technical: Three papers show steering vectors unrelated to safety, random (P3568) or learned from benign data (P0690, P3541), raise jailbreak or harmful compliance rates, linked by P0690 to interference with the refusal subspace, while P0422 shows the cost can be separated and largely removed.
items.why: Solid by the literature rule. Three separate papers report it, all with rubric C yes in papers.json, over Falcon, Llama and Qwen (P3568), Gemma, Llama, Qwen and an API model (P0690) and Gemma, Llama and Mistral (P3541).
items.note: P0422 does not contradict it. It accepts the safety cost and reports a correction that substantially reduces it. I did not read every steering paper for a report of no safety cost, so the no-counterexample condition rests on the side-effects cluster and a keyword search. It is the safety face of the side-effects cluster (97 papers). Merged from 3 verified findings across cross-cutting, persona-sycophancy, refusal-safety (open27, pers08, rste21). The family readers placed these under new, solid; the editor placed the merged item under solid. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0422).

items.title: Surface features appear early, meaning later, last layer rarely best
items.line: Language and word form become readable in the first layers, meaning and feeling later, and the final layer is seldom the best place to read.
items.status: 10 papers, 5 with a measured intervention, 7 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

quote.text: final-layer representations are rarely optimal for recovering psycholinguistic information with linear probes

items.technical: Language identity jumps from layer 0 to 1, lexical identity fades with depth while inflection persists, literal and figurative uses split early, affective features peak later, and final-layer probes are rarely optimal.
items.why: Solid by the literature rule, with one flagged disagreement. 10 papers in the family report it, 7 with held-out accuracy (rubric B yes) and 5 with a measured intervention (rubric C yes), over 10 open model families. P0696 places language-specific structure in late layers, but it measures separation between language vectors rather than whether language can be read at all, and its probes pass 99 percent from layer 14 of 32.
items.note: P1861 finds language vectors steer best at earlier layers than abstract behaviours, which fits the reading profile. P3005 finds Arabic word morphology in lower and middle layers and syntax higher, P3050 finds middle layers best for verb-particle types, and P1735 finds single-token SAE features concentrate in early layers. P0696 finds language vectors most separable at layers 22 to 32, including the last, so for language the final layer is not always a poor place to read.

items.title: Numbers and sums are stored along straight lines
items.line: Number size, digits and arithmetic steps can be read off hidden states with a simple straight-line reader.
items.status: 10 papers, 5 with a measured intervention, 5 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: [task-reasoning] peak probe accuracy for addition signals
[other] Success of adding the number direction (P0364)

quote.text: each signal family becomes linearly decodable with high accuracy (stage-wise peaks typically ≥95% on in-domain multi-digit addition, and up to 99%)

items.technical: Linear, logistic or circular probes decode formula structure, carries, digit values, counts and numeric attributes from residual activations with high held-out accuracy (stage-wise peaks of 95 to 99 percent for multi-digit addition in Llama-3-8B, R2 above 0.8 for numeric attributes), in Llama, Mistral, Qwen and Gemma models.
items.why: Six family papers, three with held-out accuracy (B yes), across Llama, Mistral, Qwen and Gemma. The limits are stated in the papers.
items.note: P0593 finds a plain single-vector linear probe poor for digits where circular and logistic probes work, and P1387 finds its latitude direction weak. Most of these studies use one or two models. Merged from 2 verified findings across task-reasoning, other (task20, othe00). Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P0477, P0593, P1387).

items.title: Probe scores work as cheap switches in real pipelines
items.line: A probe's score can decide when to retrieve, which model to call, when to stop or when to re-ask, saving compute with little accuracy loss.
items.status: 10 papers, 4 with a measured intervention, 7 with held-out accuracy

quote.text: reducing inference cost by up to 70

items.technical: Hidden-state probe outputs used as gates for routing, early exit, retrieval triggering, classifier-guided decoding, abstention or re-prompting cut cost or hallucination in the reported settings.
items.why: Solid because 10 papers report it, 7 with held-out accuracy (B yes) and 4 with a measured intervention (C yes), the coded model families of these papers span 7 families (DeepSeek, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, OLMo, Phi, Qwen), and no paper in the family shows it failing.
items.note: These are application results on the authors' own benchmarks, and none is tested under the cross-dataset shifts that break detectors in the transfer finding.

items.title: Task vectors sit in a few heads and middle layers
items.line: The task is carried by a small set of attention heads, and adding it works best in the early to middle layers.
items.status: 10 papers, 10 with a measured intervention, 2 with held-out accuracy, 2 against

quote.text: find strong causal effects across settings in middle layers

items.technical: Causal mediation and ablation place function vectors in a small set of attention heads whose ablation hurts few-shot ICL more than ablating induction heads, and injection effects peak in early to middle layers (about a third of depth for function vectors, an intermediate layer for task vectors) in GPT-J, Pythia, Llama, Qwen and Gemma models.
items.why: Ten papers with measured interventions (C yes) across five or more model families. The contrary evidence is qualified. P1105 shows that trained vectors, not extracted ones, work at any layer, and P0204 finds the head pattern varies by model.
items.note: Many of these papers pick the layer by sweeping on the evaluation data (see the settings finding), so the middle-layer pattern is firmer than any exact best layer.

items.title: Contrast directions nudge models toward preferred and obedient answers
items.line: Adding a direction built from good versus bad answer pairs raises preference scores and keeps models on the original instruction under injection.
items.status: 8 papers, 8 with a measured intervention, 4 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

numbers.label: Net win change of one hh-rlhf CAA vector on four tasks, Llama-3.2-1B (P3161 baseline)

quote.text: we derive a one-dimensional activation steering vector that increases adherence to the original instruction, suppressing the execution of injected payloads while preserving general instruction-following ability.

items.technical: Mean-difference, PCA or few-shot activation directions from preferred versus dispreferred or clean versus overwritten pairs, injected at inference or distilled into adapters, raise AlpacaEval, Arena-Hard, reward-benchmark, semantic-consistency and instruction-adherence scores and cut prompt-injection overwrites, with gains that depend on task and model.
items.why: Solid. At least 3 papers with C yes over at least 2 families, and the negative cases are reported and discussed by their authors. Counts. 8 supporting papers, 4 with rubric B yes, 8 with rubric C yes, 7 open model families (API-only families not counted), 2 from 2026, 2 against or limiting.
items.note: P3161 reports its CAA and ITI baselines going negative on several tasks, and P3541 finds benign steering erodes safety, so the gains are not free. P0573 chose control layers on the evaluation benchmark (lt_coding swept-test). P3317 finds the push raises instruction following regardless of which role gave the instruction, so it is not hierarchy-specific. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P3161).

items.title: Trained task vectors beat vectors read off the activations
items.line: Vectors tuned by gradient descent to do the task work better than vectors simply averaged from examples, most clearly for questions about images.
items.status: 9 papers, 9 with a measured intervention, 1 with held-out accuracy

quote.text: we propose directly training Learned Task Vectors (LTVs), which surpass extracted TVs in accuracy

items.technical: Task vectors optimised against a task loss (learned task vectors, LIVE, M2IV, calibrated I2CL context vectors, fine-tuned function vectors, adaptive task vectors) outperform extracted task vectors, function vectors and PCA in-context vectors on text classification, function regression and visual question answering, where plain extracted vectors fail.
items.why: Nine papers with measured interventions (C yes, P1105 also B yes) across Llama, Qwen, GPT-2, Pythia and vision-language models, and no paper shows extracted vectors ahead.
items.note: Trained vectors are close to small adapters, so their success says less about how the model itself stores the task. Every comparison is run by the authors of the trained method. Extracted vectors with selected heads (P1466) or cross-modal patching (P1224) do work in vision-language models, so the gap is about plain averaging. P0377 finds a vector trained on one CVQA region falls to about zero-shot level on the other.

items.title: Moral judgments and ethical frameworks are readable on benchmarks
items.line: Whether a case is judged right or wrong, and which moral outlook it uses, can be read off the model's state on new benchmark items.
items.status: 7 papers, 6 with a measured intervention, 5 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: moral reasoning-style direction AUC on the benchmark test set, Qwen

quote.text: On the benchmark test set, the style probe achieves 1.000 accuracy and Dir-A projections separate style labels with AUC = 1.000

items.technical: Linear probes and mean-difference directions classify held-out ETHICS, Moral Stories, Social Chemistry, moral-foundation and ethical-framework items well (style AUC 1.000 on Qwen, bootstrap-stable foundation directions on OLMo), and steering along them shifts judgments, on Qwen, Mistral, Llama, OLMo, Gemma and DeepSeek.
items.why: Solid on benchmarks. 5 papers report held-out accuracy (rubric B yes, P0420, P2181, P3402, P0611, P0819) and 6 a measured intervention, on at least Qwen, Mistral, Llama, OLMo and Gemma, and no family paper shows the reading failing in distribution.
items.note: P0420, P2181 and P3402 are among the 8 family papers with a stability check (rubric A yes). Benchmark readability may partly reflect wording (next finding). P3402 finds framework steering changes which framework a reply invokes more than the action chosen. P1544 (rubric B and C no) reads ETHICS morality with a logistic-regression axis inside a study of whether the model can control that axis, so it is weaker support.

items.title: Simple arrows detect topic and domain very well
items.line: A difference of means or a linear probe tells topics, domains and text sources apart about as well as a fine-tuned classifier.
items.status: 8 papers, 3 with a measured intervention, 7 with held-out accuracy

quote.text: For concept detection, representation-based methods such as difference-in-means, perform the best.

items.technical: Difference-of-means and logistic-probe directions reach top concept-detection AUROC on AxBench, near fine-tuned accuracy on ESG topics, and saturate math, code and text domain routing on held-out items.
items.why: Solid by the literature rule. 8 papers in the family report it, 7 with held-out accuracy (rubric B yes) and 3 with a measured intervention (rubric C yes), over 8 open model families (BERT-family, DeepSeek, GPT-2, Gemma, Llama, Mistral, Pythia/GPT-NeoX, Qwen).
items.note: Detection under shift is weaker. P0434 finds out-of-distribution generalization varies substantially (GSM8K against MATH500) and P1176 finds one SAE latent falls from 0.99 to 0.64 AUC when the prompts are translated to French.

items.title: Planted or hidden behaviours leave a readable trace
items.line: Backdoors, hidden secrets, planted goals and reward hacking show up as directions that probes catch, unless the model is trained to hide from the probe.
items.status: 8 papers, 4 with a measured intervention, 6 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

numbers.label: Backdoor isolation score, Diff-SAE versus crosscoder (P1698)
Harmfulness-probe recall under obfuscation attacks (P3708)

quote.text: monitor recall collapses to near zero while probe recall remains high (0.80–0.95), demonstrating that internal representations retain hack-relevant information after the token-level monitor has been deceived.

items.technical: Difference-based SAEs, linear probes, mean-difference directions and residual atlases isolate backdoor triggers, steganographic secrets, planted LoRA objectives, reward-hacking intent and misaligned reasoning with high held-out accuracy, and probes keep recall after a text monitor has been fooled, while sparse crosscoders and per-target SAEs often miss the planted signal, but when an attacker controls training or optimises inputs against the monitor, obfuscated activations can drive probe recall to zero and fool latent backdoor detectors (P3708).
items.why: Solid when the model is not trained against the probe. At least 3 papers with B yes over at least 2 families, and failures are specific to sparse dictionary variants or to an attacker who optimises against the monitor. Counts. 8 supporting papers, 6 with rubric B yes, 4 with rubric C yes, 8 open model families (API-only families not counted), 7 from 2026, 1 against or limiting.
items.note: Seven of the eight papers are from 2026. The limit is method-specific, since crosscoders (P1698) and per-target SAE and crosscoder baselines (P2552) fail where difference-based reads succeed. P1698 uses one small model (SmolLM2-360M), whose family is not coded. P3708 (a recall addition with no taxonomy row) shows the trace can be hidden by an attacker who optimises against the latent monitor, and even data poisoning alone achieves some obfuscation. In P3600 the model was trained against a text monitor only. P2966, outside this family, finds agents told about an activation monitor are still caught (P2966.txt line 30).

items.title: Political leaning is a readable, steerable direction in US politics
items.line: Models carry a left-right political direction that can be read to rate slant and pushed to make text more liberal or conservative.
items.status: 8 papers, 7 with a measured intervention, 3 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: lawmaker-fitted probe on news-outlet slant, Spearman by model
partisan probe cross-validated AUC, Llama 3.1 8B layer 18

quote.text: Using probes only trained to predict lawmakers’ ideology, we then show that the same probes can predict measures of news outlets’ slant from the activations of models prompted to simulate text from those news outlets.

items.why: Solid within US politics. 3 papers report held-out accuracy (rubric B yes, P0982, P0080, P2776) and 7 a measured intervention, on Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen and DeepSeek, and the failures reported lie outside this setting and are stated by the papers.

items.title: Task vectors can be added to build combined tasks

quote.text: the vector for a complex task can be approximated by adding the vectors of its constituent subtasks

items.title: Context-against-memory conflicts can be read and steered

quote.text: they can internally register the signals of knowledge conflict at mid-layers.

items.technical: Knowledge conflicts between context and parametric memory are linearly detectable at mid layers (about 80 percent at layer 13 of Llama-3-8B), and SAE-based or mean-difference edits switch answers between contextual and memorised knowledge, including 99.3 percent of colour predictions moved from priors to image evidence in vision-language models.

items.title: Steering is neither hidden from the model nor automatically safe

quote.text: After fine-tuning, seven instruction-tuned models develop strong steering awareness on heldout concepts; the best reaches 95.5% detection, 71.2% concept identification, and zero false positives on clean inputs.

items.why: Solid by the count rule. At least 3 papers with C yes over at least 2 families for each half and none contrary, but all are from 2026. Counts. 8 supporting papers, 1 with rubric B yes, 8 with rubric C yes, 8 open model families (API-only families not counted), 8 from 2026, 0 against or limiting.

P0426 adds that detection-trained models are more susceptible to steering, not less. Detection or resistance rests on three papers (P0426, P1288, P1253). Safety erosion rests on P3541 and P3568 in this family plus P0422 and P0486 from the refusal family, and P1739 is an attack on turn count. P0422 finds the safety cost sits in a separable component that can be removed, so the erosion is not unavoidable.

items.technical: Four 2026 papers that select the layer or setting on the evaluation data also rerun the selection with the evaluation data held out and find little inflation, a nested cross-validation bias of +0.005 on Qwen2-7B and -0.026 on GPT-2-Large (P3560), a nested reanalysis dropping AUC by 0.01 on average and at most 0.07 (P3106), recovery that stays clear of baseline when the layer and coefficient are picked on a dev half (P2801) and source-condition gains that hold on held-out questions for every model (P2943), against 235 papers that sweep and report on the test or do not say.
