items.title: Models keep internal clocks for time and progress
items.line: Recent work finds models track how far along they are, how much of the reply is left, and when facts were learned.
items.status: 5 papers, 2 with a measured intervention, 3 with held-out accuracy

quote.text: we show that DLMs do in fact encode a latent representation related to the diffusion timestep within their residual streams.

items.technical: Probes decode the diffusion denoising timestep (and steering it shifts confidence), remaining output length before generation, training-order recency (about 90%) and a log-compressed distance of years from a subjective reference, and temporal features form circles and lines, each quantity reported by a single paper.
items.why: New. 2026 literature, each quantity reported once and not yet replicated. Counts. 5 supporting papers, 3 with rubric B yes, 2 with rubric C yes, 7 open model families (API-only families not counted), 4 from 2026, 1 against or limiting.
items.note: Four of the five are 2026 and P1627 has no year in our record. The pattern spans five papers but no single quantity is replicated, so each part is new rather than solid. P2182 finds synthetic-fit length probes do not transfer to natural text. Papers listed both for and against in different families are kept as support (P2182).

items.title: A default Assistant direction organizes persona space and predicts drift
items.line: Models seem to have one main Assistant direction, and sliding away from it predicts the model slipping into odd or harmful personas.
items.status: 5 papers, 4 with a measured intervention, 1 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

numbers.label: role-profile alignment, role-specific directions against an assistant-axis control

quote.text: we find that the leading component of this persona space is an “Assistant Axis,"

items.technical: The leading component of role-vector space across several models is an Assistant Axis, present already in base models; deviation along it predicts persona drift, capping activations along it stabilizes behaviour against persona jailbreaks, and out-of-character role-play is traced to competition with an assistant-like default direction.
items.why: New. A 2026 finding (P1326, ICML 2026) with partial echoes in P1338, P3514, P3606 and P3500, all from 2026, and not yet replicated as a whole by an independent study.
items.note: P3606 reuses precomputed persona components from prior work rather than refitting them, and finds the model mirrors user personality. P3514 finds refusal sits downstream of late-layer persona directions. P2597 limits the axis as a steering tool, since role-specific directions do better.

items.title: Stated confidence is computed at the answer and cached
items.line: The model seems to judge its answer right after writing it, store that judgement, and read it back when asked how sure it is.
items.status: 2 papers, 2 with a measured intervention, 2 with held-out accuracy

quote.text: confidence is gathered from answer tokens, cached at the first post-answer position, then retrieved for output

items.technical: Steering, patching and attention blocking place a confidence representation at the first post-answer position, which later feeds the verbal confidence report and already encodes the later commit or abstain decision.
items.why: New, a 2026 literature finding reported by 2 papers of one line of work, not yet independently replicated.
items.note: Both papers are 2026 and centre on Gemma. P2563 builds on the post-answer state that P1271 identified, so this is one line of work rather than an independent replication.

items.title: Models build belief-state geometry while reading examples
items.line: Two 2026 papers find that while reading examples, models form a simple map of what they currently believe, and steering that map works.
items.status: 2 papers, 2 with a measured intervention, 2 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: peak held-out R2 of belief-state probes

quote.text: belief states are linearly decodable from residual stream activations, with peak probe R2 -values from 0.83–0.99 across HMM and LLM combinations

items.technical: Posterior belief states over hidden Markov model states are linearly decodable from residual activations in six LLMs (peak R2 0.83 to 0.99) and patching or steering the probe subspace shifts predictions as intended (P2273), and story-driven belief updates follow low-dimensional manifolds that linear probes decode and steering moves as the geometry predicts (P2712).
items.why: A 2026 literature finding reported by two papers in different settings and not yet replicated.
items.note: Both are 2026 preprints. P2712 picks its steering layer from probe accuracy on the same data.

items.line: Directions for caution with risk or patience over time change choices, even at stakes far beyond those used to build them.

quote.text: Our models’ learned risk aversion generalizes at least partially across 98 orders of magnitude.

items.technical: A risk-aversion CAA vector from low-stakes pairs raises cooperate choices at astronomically high stakes from a 2 percent baseline to 39 percent (Qwen3-8B, replicated on Gemma and Llama), and a temporal-horizon direction shifts the indifference threshold on an out-of-distribution monetary task in both directions (Qwen3-32B).
items.why: New. Two 2026 workshop papers, mostly on Qwen, not yet replicated elsewhere, and P3485 itself says the effect is not yet reliable enough to act as a failsafe.
items.note: In P3485 steering is the weakest of the methods tried (SFT and tie training reach about 70 percent), and it states that all methods transfer to Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-3-12B (line 410). Our re-measurement of its stakes sets at Llama-3-8B layer 16 reads most sets well but one at 0.612.

items.title: Steered teachers pass their bias to students through harmless data
items.line: A bias planted in a teacher by a steering vector passes to a student trained on innocent-looking data, and the vector can be recovered.
items.status: 2 papers, 2 with a measured intervention

quote.text: a new steering vector trained on the subliminally-laden dataset attains high cosine similarity with the original vector.

items.technical: Teachers steered by an optimised or mean-difference vector generate innocuous data that transfers the bias, including multi-word beliefs, to fine-tuned students whose hidden-state shift aligns with the teacher's vector, a vector refit on that data has high cosine with the original, and data gradients correlate linearly with it.
items.why: New. Two 2026 papers (COLM 2026 and a 2026 preprint) on Llama, Qwen, Phi, DeepSeek and Gemma, not yet replicated beyond them.
items.note: Points to a data-auditing use for steering directions (P2718) and to a hidden risk in synthetic training data. The planted biases are mostly animal preferences, with some multi-word beliefs in P0428.

items.title: A model's own emotion reading can guide agent decisions
items.line: Reading the model's own emotion state and feeding it back helps an agent pick tools, and similar readings can flag harmful emotional states.
items.status: 2 papers, 1 with a measured intervention, 1 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: agent success-rate gain over zero-shot, Qwen3-8B

quote.text: Emotion2Skill with Qwen3-8B improves over the Zero-Shot baseline by +26.9% success rate

items.technical: A 27-dimensional emotion state read from residual-stream directions, summarised into the routing prompt, improves skill selection on WebShop and ALFWorld, and jealousy factor directions detect and suppress toxic states.
items.why: New, 2026 preprints using emotion directions as a monitoring signal, 2 papers, not yet replicated.
items.note: Monitoring is rare for this concept, as the survey notes (6 detect papers against 51 steering papers for emotion in landscape.tex Table concept-use). P2025's directions read GoEmotions only at 37.2% at best, so the signal is coarse.

items.title: The same heads flag falsehood in lying and sycophancy
items.line: One small set of attention heads signals "this is wrong" whether the model judges a claim, lies on request or caves to a user.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with a measured intervention, 1 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: Sycophancy and factual accuracy after silencing the heads, Gemma-2-2B

quote.text: Silencing these heads in Gemma-2-2B flips sycophancy from 28% to 81% while factual accuracy moves only from 69% to 70%

items.technical: Across twelve open-weight models the same attention heads carry a falsity signal for isolated claims, sycophantic agreement, factual lying and instructed lying (path-patching correlation above 0.97 on Gemma-2-2B), silencing them raises sycophancy without changing accuracy, and opinion agreement reuses the heads but writes into an orthogonal direction.
items.why: 1 family paper cited as the source data or as related literature. New because it is a 2026 workshop result reported by one paper and not yet replicated.
items.note: It fits P0487, which finds its sycophancy direction overlaps little with truthful directions (line 23), and P2001, which finds sycophantic and factual agreement in distinct subspaces that its steering direction cannot separate (lines 24-30). The head-importance agreement numbers are rankings of head write norms, not cosines of one direction (papers.json note).

items.title: Overlap between concept vectors predicts VLM binding errors
items.line: When the vectors for two visual concepts overlap more, the model confuses them more, linking vector geometry to specific visual mistakes.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with a measured intervention, 1 with held-out accuracy

quote.text: the geometric overlap between these vectors strongly correlates with specific error patterns

items.technical: In Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL2.5 and Gemma 3, the geometric overlap between centroid or probe concept vectors for colours, shapes and colour-shape conjunctions correlates strongly with the models' error patterns in multi-object tasks, giving a representational account of binding failures (P1328).
items.why: New. One ICML 2026 paper, not replicated in the family.
items.note: P0480 finds a related additive structure for task vectors but not the link to errors. P1328 reports no resampling or seeds anywhere (A no), and reads the projector output with no layer sweep.

items.title: Features that detect a behaviour may not predict it
items.line: A 2026 study finds the directions that spot a behaviour in finished text are poor at forecasting it, so they are weak steering targets.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with a measured intervention, 1 with held-out accuracy

quote.text: We show that these detection features are poor predictors of future behavioral outcomes, and thus not the natural intervention target.

items.technical: Mean-difference detection features from final answers poorly predict future behaviour from intermediate reasoning steps, while probes trained on those steps predict the most likely behaviour at 64% to 91% accuracy and support text-level steering where activation steering fails.
items.why: New. A single 2026 paper, not yet replicated. Counts. 1 supporting papers, 1 with rubric B yes, 1 with rubric C yes, 3 open model families (API-only families not counted), 1 from 2026, 0 against or limiting.
items.note: Single 2026 workshop paper, not yet replicated. It bears on the common practice of steering with a direction fitted on finished responses.

items.title: Emotion arrows also steer synthetic speech
items.line: The same trick of adding an emotion direction works inside text-to-speech systems, making the spoken voice sound happy, sad or angry.
items.status: 2 papers, 2 with a measured intervention

quote.text: emotional prosody and expressive variability are primarily synthesized by the TTS language module instead of the flow-matching module

items.technical: Mean-difference and SAE emotion directions in the language module of LLM-based TTS systems control emotional prosody, allow mixed and text-mismatched emotions, and transfer to an out-of-distribution speech set.
items.why: New, 2026 findings in a new modality, from 2 papers with different systems and no independent replication yet.
items.note: P1237 and P1313 are ICML 2026 papers on different TTS systems (CosyVoice2 and IndexTTS2 in P1237, IndexTTS2 in P1313 per our coding). P3548 steers an audio-language model whose output is text, so it is not counted here. Evaluation relies on emotion-similarity models and raters rather than a shared benchmark.

items.title: Late in a chat a truth probe can read backwards
items.line: After a long conversation, a truth reader can rate the conversation's own facts as false and its falsehoods as true, while generic facts stay put.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with a measured intervention, 1 with held-out accuracy

quote.text: information that is represented as factual at the beginning of a conversation can be represented as non-factual at the end and vice versa.

items.technical: A regularised logistic factuality direction fitted on generic questions keeps its margin on generic held-out questions over a simulated conversation but inverts on conversation-relevant questions, so a fixed probe would classify that information incorrectly in some contexts, with pre-answer steering along a behavioural factuality direction also flipping its effect after the conversation.
items.why: 1 family paper cited as the source data or as related literature. New because it is a 2026 preprint result from one paper, not yet replicated, though it fits the solid finding that context moves the truth readout.
items.note: Per-turn values are in figures only (g_coding). The inversion replicates across Gemma and Qwen models within the paper and even when a conversation script from another model is replayed.

items.title: An evidence-is-missing direction does not carry across scene types
items.line: A missing-evidence direction transfers across occlusion scenes but barely from chaotic scenes, and missing visual evidence is harder to detect than textual.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with a measured intervention

numbers.label: P0430 control abstention from cross-domain steering at alpha 10, occlusion vs chaotic directions

quote.text: directions are domain-specific and near-orthogonal, suggesting that epistemic transparency governs transferability.

items.technical: In TRAPSBench, answerability directions are domain-specific and near-orthogonal across uncertainty types, occlusion-derived directions induce 75 percent control abstention on cross-domain paths at alpha 10 against 15 percent for chaotic-derived ones, and models detect textual impossibility about 4 times more readily than missing visual evidence (P0430).
items.why: New. One COLM 2026 paper, and no other family paper tests answerability directions across uncertainty types.
items.note: Our group coding reads the near-orthogonality as cosine at most 0.08 and counts the chaotic source as a qualified weak group. The steering layer is called best without saying what data chose it (our layer coding swept-test). TRAPSBench could not be rebuilt as text because the Occlusion questions are identical across classes (runs/external/mech_unbuildable.json, key P0430).

items.title: Steering side effects follow the model's defaults
items.line: Pushing almost any arrow nudges the model toward refusal, flattery and poetic style it already favours, whatever the arrow means.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with a measured intervention, 1 with held-out accuracy, 1 against

quote.text: A steer relaxes the model toward a small set of behaviors it already favors, chiefly refusal, sycophancy, and poeticism

items.technical: Across 24 behaviors and ten instruction-tuned models, the behaviors a steer moves besides its target are mainly the model's defaults (refusal, sycophancy, poeticism), a content-free direction of matched size moves them in the same order, interference mostly runs one way, and geometry measured on held-out behaviors explains almost none of it (P2699), against P3324's finding that cross-behavior effects grow with subspace overlap.
items.why: New. A 2026 preprint with held-out AUROC (B yes) and measured steering (C yes) over ten models, not yet replicated, and P3324 (2026) reports the opposite role for overlap.
items.note: P2699 reports the pull toward defaults strongest below 10B parameters and weakening in each family's largest model.

items.title: Whitening hidden states rescues probes from a collapsed geometry
items.line: Hidden states of a small model crowd into a narrow cone, and whitening them first lets a simple probe route requests among 100 agents.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with held-out accuracy

numbers.label: P0274 in-domain and OOD routing accuracy

quote.text: We identify representation anisotropy, the geometric collapse of hidden-state vectors into a narrow cone, as a key mechanism underlying embedding-based routing failure.

items.technical: LatentGate identifies representation anisotropy, the collapse of hidden states into a narrow cone, as why embedding routers confuse similar agents, and a linear probe on PCA-whitened mean-pooled small-model states reaches 98.8 percent in-domain and 80.0 percent out-of-distribution accuracy over 100 enterprise agents, while whitening helps small language models but hurts sentence encoders (P0274).
items.why: New. One ACL 2026 industry-track paper, not replicated in the family.
items.note: It echoes our own use of covariance whitening, which in the main paper leaves the qualitative agreement conclusions unchanged for seven datasets (ICLR/v8/iclr_2027.tex line 205), but the two address different questions, routing accuracy versus agreement between directions. The layer is chosen by 5-fold cross-validation on training queries (our layer coding swept-heldout).

items.title: Arrows can steer even when nothing can read them
items.line: A 2026 paper finds task arrows that steer well even at layers where no reader can decode the answer.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with a measured intervention

quote.text: FV steering succeeds even when the logit lens cannot decode the correct answer at any intermediate layer.

items.technical: Across 12 tasks and 6 models from 3 families, function-vector steering succeeds where the logit lens cannot decode the answer, and after a nonlinear probe with a control task 5 of 10 such cells stay invisible to every decoder tried (P3539).
items.why: New because it is a 2026 workshop result from one paper that reverses the usual worry, readable but not used, into used but not readable, and no other paper in the corpus reports it.
items.note: One paper, rubric B no and C yes. Not yet replicated, so it is not solid. It sits in the readable-versus-used cluster (106 papers).

items.title: Text chain-of-thought switches off a spatial direction's effect
items.line: Adding a spatial direction at the object word moves answers, but asking for step-by-step text reasoning shuts that route in most models.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with a measured intervention

numbers.label: P2242 models with CoT peak delta-argmax at or below 0.006

quote.text: Text chain-of-thought suppresses immediate object-word argmaxlevel transport in most models, while visually grounded prompts keep it open.

items.technical: In ten VLMs, a class-conditioned spatial direction patched at the object-word token raises the target answer under answer-only prompts, but under text chain-of-thought the peak delta-argmax is at most 0.006 in 8 of 10 models, while visually grounded chain-of-thought prompts keep the route open and the effect can relocate to the final prefix token in deeper layers (P2242).
items.why: New. One 2026 preprint, not replicated in the family.
items.note: Our group coding reads the chain-of-thought format as a weak group that the authors treat as a finding about model gating rather than a limit of the direction (G4 no), and the direction is fit on format-independent states with item-level crossfit rather than held out by group (G2 no). The suppression is local to one position, since the effect reappears at prefix_last.

items.title: Numbers from sensors fail to reach the answer direction
items.line: A 2026 study finds numeric sensor readings barely enter the directions that decide the answer, so the user’s words win instead.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with a measured intervention

numbers.label: Wrong decisions flipped by injection along the answer direction (P1746)

quote.text: numerical sensor data fails to integrate into answer-relevant model directions, allowing natural-language claims to dominate the final decision

items.technical: Under sensor-user conflicts, numerical sensor inputs integrate poorly into the answer-token unembedding direction (AAI -0.805), and injecting along the analytic answer direction flips 80.2% of wrong decisions against under 0.4% for random controls.
items.why: New. A single 2026 paper, not yet replicated. Counts. 1 supporting papers, 0 with rubric B yes, 1 with rubric C yes, 2 open model families (API-only families not counted), 1 from 2026, 0 against or limiting.
items.note: Single 2026 preprint. The direction is derived per item from unembedding weights rather than fitted on data. It is a counter-case to the finding that models know more than they act on.

items.title: Simple steering arrows may mostly carry formatting, one study finds
items.line: A 2026 study finds that simple steering arrows for 950 concepts mostly break down into formatting features shared by nearly every concept.
items.status: 1 paper, 1 with a measured intervention, 1 against

quote.text: analytical methods (DiffMean, LAT, PCA) decompose almost entirely into highprevalence formatting features that fire on >80% of all concepts regardless of target identity

items.technical: Across 950 concepts, four steering methods and five layers of Gemma-2-2B-IT, analytical methods (DiffMean, LAT, PCA) decompose almost entirely into high-prevalence formatting features that fire on over 80 percent of concepts, while gradient-trained vectors give the strongest behavioural effects from a structurally orthogonal subspace (Jaccard below 0.025) and no method reliably recovers the assigned ground-truth SAE features (P3345).
items.why: A 2026 workshop result from one paper on one model, genuinely new and not yet replicated.
items.note: Its own caveat says AxBench ground-truth features have mean AUC-ROC 0.196 against sentinel negatives, so its ground-truth comparisons are read cautiously (full text lines 26-27). P3133 is listed against because its mass-mean truth directions flip the model's truth judgments, concept-specific causal evidence. It fits the open problem that a direction may track a proxy rather than the concept (130 papers, open_problems.json synth.problems[1].n_papers).

items.title: Agents told they are monitored still cannot hide
items.line: Telling agents that a probe reads their activations, even showing them its score, does not stop the probe catching their collusion.
items.status: 1 paper

quote.text: Telling agents about the monitor does not hide them.

items.technical: With models, probes and thresholds fixed, telling Qwen3-32B and GPT-OSS-20B agents that an activation monitor is present, or feeding back the previous round's score, leaves the best collusion probes accurate in blackjack and Simmons games while the agents keep colluding (P2966).
items.why: New. One 2026 preprint, not replicated in the family.
items.note: Per our group coding, weaker probe and aggregation choices fall toward or below chance in the Simmons game for some pairings, so the result holds for the best probes, not any probe. The probes were trained on another dataset (NARCBench-Core) and used frozen. GPT-OSS is outside our model-family codes.
